summary: Iteration 4 — Shared pool + BoB effective date filter + Leads no-refresh + PATCH /shared-leads/{id} bug-fix verification. Backend: 12/12 tests pass (added 4 new tests for the dedicated PATCH endpoint covering lock-holder success, non-holder 423, Complete auto-claim + BoB visibility, and 404). Frontend: uncovered a NEW CRITICAL bug that prevents agents from opening any shared-lead detail page in the running preview build — a race caused by React 18 StrictMode + the unmount-cleanup unlock in SharedLeadDetail.jsx.

ui_bugs.issue: Race condition: the unmount-cleanup calls release() unconditionally, sending POST /shared-leads/{id}/unlock via fetch(keepalive). Under React 18 StrictMode (enabled in /src/index.js and running under craco start dev server on the preview URL), the effect mounts → cleans up → mounts again on the very first navigation. The cleanup's async unlock races with the bootstrap's Promise.all([GET /shared-leads/{id}, GET /statuses]) and arrives at the server BEFORE the GET, so the GET returns 423 'You must claim this lead first' and the user is bounced back to /shared-leads with an error toast. Backend logs confirmed the sequence: lock 200 → lock 200 → lock 200 → unlock 200 → GET 423. This is reproducible 100% of the time when an agent clicks any Available row in the shared pool.

action_items: CRITICAL — Fix SharedLeadDetail.jsx race: gate the effect-cleanup release() so it only fires on true unmount/page-unload, not on StrictMode remount. Options: (a) split the beforeunload listener into its own effect with no cleanup-release, (b) skip the cleanup release() when releasedRef.current has just been set (add a short-lived guard), or (c) simplest: only release inside the beforeunload handler and inside the explicit releaseAndLeave button, remove the release() call at line 84 of the cleanup. Also consider making the unlock endpoint idempotent-with-serverside-sequencing (e.g. only unlock if lock is still held by same user AND lock_seq matches).
Add data-testid='quick-status-{id}' to the inline row Select on Leads.jsx around line 419 so per-row status changes can be automated (currently only accessible via generic [role='combobox']).
Re-run frontend Playwright scenarios for shared-pool status change + Complete flow once the race is fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: SharedLeadDetail.jsx — unmount-cleanup unlock is the classic StrictMode footgun: async cleanup that mutates server state races with concurrent bootstrap requests. It's also fragile in production if the user navigates rapidly.
Backend PATCH /shared-leads/{lead_id} is well-designed — locking as authorisation, auto-claim on Complete, agents blocked from reassigning. Confirmed by 4 new pytest cases.
SharedLeadDetail bootstrap POSTs /lock even when the list page already locked it in openLead(); the second POST is idempotent server-side so this is harmless but wastes a round-trip.

rca of the issue: React 18 StrictMode double-invokes effects in development. The useEffect at SharedLeadDetail.jsx:65-86 registers a beforeunload listener AND returns a cleanup that calls release() (which POSTs unlock via fetch keepalive). On first render, the cleanup fires between the two mount cycles. `releasedRef.current` gets set to true, so the second cleanup is a no-op — but the DB has already been unlocked. Meanwhile the bootstrap effect at :25 has issued POST /lock (200) and is waiting on Promise.all([GET /shared-leads/{id}, GET /statuses]). The unlock arrives at the server between the lock and the GET (server logs prove this: lock, lock, lock, unlock, GET 423). Mitigation: remove the release() call from the cleanup (line 84) and rely on the explicit releaseAndLeave button + beforeunload handler; OR move the beforeunload registration to its own effect with no cleanup side-effect; OR gate release() with a mounted-duration guard (`if (Date.now() - mountedAt < 500) return`).
